question.text: The modulus of the complex number $z$ such that $|z+3-i|=1$ and $\arg (z)=\pi$ is equal to

solution.text: Let $z=x+i y$ Given, $\quad|z+3-i|=1$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad|(x+3)+(y-1) i|=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2=1\ldots(i) \end{aligned}$ Above is the equation of circle with centre $\equiv(-3,1)$ and $\text { radius }=1$ Also, $\arg (z)=\pi \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|=\pi$ $\Rightarrow \quad\left|\frac{y}{x}\right|=\tan \pi=0 \Rightarrow y=0$ By Eq. (i), $\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & x & =-3 \\ \therefore & z & =-3+0 i \\ \Rightarrow & \text { Modulus of } z & =3 \end{aligned}$
